freediving.verdict: The widest door on this map and a genuine ladder above it, with three of its four named people there for having founded the place rather than for teaching in it

conditions.n: Is there a teacher, and can we name them?
conditions.t: Dark, and the correction is ours. Four names sit on this page and three of them are here for having founded the school: Umberto Pelizzari at the Apnea Academy, Lotta Ericson at Freedive Dahab, Stavros Kastrinakis at Kalamata. Founding a school is not teaching in it — the same reading that darkened this dot on French pastry two days before this grade was written, and the previous version of this answer offered the founder evidence as a strength. Only William Trubridge carries a teaching claim: he leads the once-yearly Master Class at Vertical Blue himself. The second way to light this answer does not open either. The course we point you at ends in an Apnea Academy Freediving Instructor certificate, which the Apnea Academy awards — AIDA and Molchanovs are real outside bodies in this craft, but the pick does not run through them. The names stay on the page; they are simply not the answer to this question.

conditions.n: Can a stranger get in, on a date you can book?
conditions.t: Open at every level, everywhere, on published dates. Beginner-to-instructor pathways in Dahab, two-to-four-week Master Programmes, a seven-day residential instructor course in the Mediterranean. And the hands can ruin it in the most literal sense on this map: this is breath-hold, the failure mode is blackout, and the buddy system is the discipline rather than the paperwork.

conditions.n: Will there be other people learning beside you?
conditions.t: Dahab is where the world's freedivers go to find each other — three schools on one bay, month-long intensives, and the Blue Hole as a shared workplace. Kalamata's competition line puts you on the same rope as people going considerably deeper than you. Both directions, on the same buoy.

conditions.n: Is the craft alive in this place, or is the school the only thing here?
conditions.t: Yes, and settled by the sport's own governing body rather than by a school. CMAS held the 8th World Championship Freediving Depth at Kalamata from 2 to 13 October 2024 — the world championship coming to the bay, organised by nobody who teaches there. What that does not settle is Dahab, which is the busiest of the four and the one nobody outside the sport has written about.

evidence.what: CMAS's own record of the 8th World Championship Freediving Depth

conditions.n: Is there enough here to keep you learning for years?
conditions.t: Nobody of ours has been. AIDA and Molchanovs both publish real ladders that run well past instructor, and the depth itself is an unarguable measure of where you are on them. But whether there is a room above you worth years — people to keep training with after the certificate — is the one thing no agency publishes, and only somebody who stayed can say.

jewelry-and-goldsmithing.verdict: Four scenes on three continents and a credential the trade reads, above benches where nobody will yet tell you whose hands you would be working under

conditions.n: Is there a teacher, and can we name them?
conditions.t: Dark, and the old answer said why without following it: Gio Carbone is 'the one named person on this page, in the school he founded'. He founded Le Arti Orafe in 1985 and nothing published says he teaches the annual course. The other three destinations — the Gemological Institute of America, Pforzheim's Goldschmiedeschule, the Indian Institute of Gems & Jewellery — name nobody at all. The second way in does not open for the school we point you at either: LAO's annual course ends in a LAO diploma, awarded by LAO. The GIA Graduate Gemologist and the German Meister are examined by somebody outside the school, and both are real — but they are at Carlsbad and Pforzheim, not at the bench in Florence we send you to. His name stays on the page. Ask LAO who will be at the bench beside you.

conditions.n: Can a stranger get in, on a date you can book?
conditions.t: Open in four countries, on published dates: LAO's annual goldsmithing course in Florence, the GIA Graduate Jeweler diploma over 28 weeks in Carlsbad, Studio Jewelers' 24-week programme in New York, Pforzheim's Berufskolleg and Meisterschule, IIGJ's manufacturing diploma in Jaipur. And your hands can ruin the work about as literally as anywhere here — solder floods, a stone chips, the piece is gone.

conditions.n: Will there be other people learning beside you?
conditions.t: The strongest thing this craft has, and the community dots above are the evidence for it rather than a second opinion. Florence and the Carlsbad–New York axis both read Legendary; Pforzheim is a town built around goldsmithing with a Meisterschule at its centre; Jaipur's Johari Bazaar is lapidary and meenakari ateliers working street by street. Four scenes, three continents, peers in all of them.

conditions.n: Is the craft alive in this place, or is the school the only thing here?
conditions.t: Yes for Pforzheim, and only there. The town has a jewellery museum of its own, the Schmuckmuseum Pforzheim — what a place keeps when the trade is the reason it exists rather than an industry that happens to be there. Jaipur and Florence we have taken on their reputations and the schools' own pages, which is not the same standard; an afternoon in either would settle it.

evidence.what: the Schmuckmuseum Pforzheim, the town's jewellery museum

conditions.n: Is there enough here to keep you learning for years?
conditions.t: Nobody of ours has been, and there is plainly more here than an attendance certificate: the GIA Graduate Gemologist is a qualification the trade reads, and the German Meister is a state-regulated title with an examination behind it. We have read that on their pages. We have not watched anyone climb it, and until we have, it stays a claim we are repeating rather than one we are making.

new-basque-cuisine.verdict: A faculty the Basque chefs built for themselves, examined by a university rather than vouched for by a teacher — and the great names beside it are a lineage, not a class

conditions.n: Is there a teacher, and can we name them?
conditions.t: Lit, but not by the names you would expect, and the difference is the whole answer. Andoni Luis Aduriz at Mugaritz and Martín Berasategui at Lasarte-Oria have moved to where the craft comes from: what they offer is a stage you apply for, not a course you book, and their own entries on this page say so — 'listed for the lineage, not as a class'. The Basque Culinary Center, which is where a stranger can actually enrol, still names no teacher. What lights this answer is the other way in: its Culinary Techniques Mastery carries 6 ECTS awarded with Mondragon University, so somebody outside the kitchen sets the standard and marks against it. That is a weaker promise than a name and a stronger one than a brochure. Ask them who runs the five weeks; the names would be worth more than the credits.

conditions.n: Can a stranger get in, on a date you can book?
conditions.t: Open at the faculty and shut at the restaurants, and the difference is the whole shape of this craft. The Basque Culinary Center runs its Culinary Techniques Mastery at about 3,320 EUR and the Escuela de Cocina Luis Irizar a two-year professional specialisation. Mugaritz and Berasategui take stagiaires on their own terms. Your hands can ruin it in either room.

conditions.n: Will there be other people learning beside you?
conditions.t: San Sebastián reads Legendary above, and the reason is not a school — it is that a town of a hundred and eighty thousand people holds one of the densest concentrations of serious kitchens in Europe, plus the faculty those kitchens founded. There is a generation above you here and one below, and they drink in the same bars.

conditions.n: Is the craft alive in this place, or is the school the only thing here?
conditions.t: Yes. San Sebastián Gastronomika fills the Kursaal in Donostia every autumn — 5–7 October in 2026 — a congress the city's own kitchens built and still fill. A town that hosts the argument about its cuisine is a town that cuisine belongs to. What we still have not done is walk the Gipuzkoa markets, which is where a week would teach more than the reading has.

conditions.n: Is there enough here to keep you learning for years?
conditions.t: Nobody of ours has been. The Basque Culinary Center's degree is awarded with Mondragon University, which is an outside body with an examination behind it — one of the better ladders on this map. We have read it. We have not seen anyone climb it.
